slides.title: Template Compilation Mechanics & Overhead
slides.prompt: Templates use a two-phase lookup model. Because code is generated per unique type combination, templates can cause compile-time slowdowns and binary size expansion (code bloat) if managed improperly.

slides.title: Two-Phase Lookup Phase 1
slides.prompt: Fill in the phase term where non-dependent names and syntax are verified when the template is first parsed.
slides.codeSnippet: // Phase ___ lookup verifies template syntax independently of concrete type arguments.

slides.title: Dependent Name Definition
slides.prompt: What is a dependent name in a C++ template?
options: A name that depends directly or indirectly on a template parameter type
A global variable declared outside template scopes
A library function loaded dynamically at runtime
slides.correctAnswer: A name that depends directly or indirectly on a template parameter type

slides.title: typename Keyword for Dependent Nested Types
slides.prompt: Fill in the required keyword preceding a dependent nested type inside a template.

slides.title: Template Code Bloat Cause
slides.prompt: What causes the phenomenon known as 'Code Bloat' in template-heavy C++ applications?
options: The compiler generates entirely duplicate machine code implementations for every unique combination of template arguments used
Templates force the compiler to include debug symbols in release builds
Template instantiations prevent link-time dead code elimination
Template definitions dynamically allocate executable heap memory
slides.correctAnswer: The compiler generates entirely duplicate machine code implementations for every unique combination of template arguments used

slides.title: Extern Template Declaration (C++11)
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used in C++11 to suppress template instantiation in the current translation unit.
slides.codeSnippet:
// Prevents automatic instantiation in this file:
___ template class std::vector<MyClass>;

slides.title: Mitigating Template Code Bloat
slides.prompt: Which technique helps mitigate template code bloat when creating container class templates?
options: Factoring out type-independent code into non-template base classes or void* internal helpers
Making all template member functions virtual
Splitting templates into multiple .cpp files without headers
Using constexpr for all template local variables
slides.correctAnswer: Factoring out type-independent code into non-template base classes or void* internal helpers

slides.title: Template Disambiguator Keyword
slides.prompt: Fill in the disambiguator keyword required when calling a dependent template member function e.g. obj.template func<T>().

slides.title: Impact of Precompiled Headers on Templates
slides.prompt: Why do precompiled headers (PCH) significantly benefit template-heavy C++ codebases?
options: They cache parsed standard library template headers, reducing redundant parsing time across translation units
They eliminate binary executable size bloat entirely
They convert template definitions directly into dynamic libraries
They defer template type deduction until runtime
slides.correctAnswer: They cache parsed standard library template headers, reducing redundant parsing time across translation units
